Neutral Experiment 2 locator metadata (p. 9, anticipatory informative pointing/communication) combined with the preserved validated sibling field scope (extractions/1586.json at commit f3eb01ce19e9a1fc79ed85fc1b0964f7ba53cf01) positively identifies the target effect as the 24–27-month-old age-matched replication group's planned paired-samples t-test on informing frequency by points and/or vocalizations across false-belief versus true-belief trials ('planned paired samples t-tests on the frequency of helping during FB and TB trials for each age group', p. 8; '2-year-olds M = 2.16' vs. 'M = 0.97', '2-year-olds: t(15) = 2.70, P < 0.05', p. 9), distinct from the pooled ANOVA (F(1,28) = 11.84), Wilcoxon signed-rank frequency tests (z = 3.25 pooled; z = 2.44 in 2-year-olds), McNemar at-least-once proportion test (11/16 vs. 5/16, P = 0.077), and the 3-year-old extension group (t(15) = 2.47). The authors' replication verdict specifically covers this 24–27-month-old informing-frequency effect ('These results replicate Knudsen and Liszkowski’s (2012) ﬁndings with 24-month-old children', p. 9; 'Two- and 3-year-old children tried to communicate with an experimenter about a relocation of her object more frequently when she had not observed the transfer, replicating Knudsen and Liszkowski (2012)', p. 9; 'One task fully replicated evidence of 2-year-old children’s sensitivity to others’ ignorance', p. 1), whereas 'partially extend them to 3-year-old children' qualifies the added 3-year-old extension and shipped 'mixed' misapplied an Abstract quote about Experiment 1's failed 18-month-old violation-of-expectation tasks.
